title: Why Is Your Brain Addicted to BAD News?
title_alternatives: Why Your Brain Remembers the BAD Things
Why One Insult Beats Ten COMPLIMENTS
The Ancient Alarm Inside Your HEAD
description:
One sad word in a headline gets more clicks. Your skin reacts to bad news before you've decided how you feel. Where does this pull come from, why did it keep our ancestors alive, and who barely has it at all? A tour through the psychology of the negativity bias, from snakes in the grass to the smoke detector principle.

This video is psychology and history, not medical or mental-health advice.

- Vaish, Grossmann & Woodward (2008). Not all emotions are created equal. Psychological Bulletin.
- Mather & Carstensen (2005). Aging and motivated cognition: the positivity effect. Trends in Cognitive Sciences.
